sec: Growth hormone physiology, secretion and obesity dynamics

items.q: What proportion of anterior pituitary cells are constituted by growth hormone-secreting somatotrophs?
items.exp: Somatotrophs account for 50% of the anterior pituitary cell population. (Book p945)

items.q: Growth hormone is a single polypeptide chain comprising ___ amino acids.
items.exp: Growth hormone contains 191 amino acids. (Book p945)

items.q: During which physiological sleep stage does the primary nocturnal surge of growth hormone occur?
items.exp: GH secretion occurs predominantly during deep slow-wave Stage 3 and 4 NREM sleep. (Book p945)

items.q: Assess the kinetics of growth hormone measurement: I A single random basal GH level is unreliable due to its pulsatile secretion and short half-life of 5 to 20 minutes. II IGF-1 and IGFBP-3 provide a stable integrated estimation with a half-life of 12 to 15 hours.
opts: Both I and II are true
Both I and II are false
items.exp: GH has a short half-life of 5-20 minutes, while IGF-1 bound to IGFBP-3 has a half-life of 12-15 hours, making it the preferred indirect measure. (Book p945)

items.q: Which circulating hormone does NOT stimulate hepatic IGF-1 synthesis independently of growth hormone?
items.exp: Thyroid hormones, insulin, and gonadal hormones independently stimulate IGF-1; cortisol does not. (Book p945)

items.q: An 8-year-old obese boy demonstrates accelerated height velocity despite paradoxically suppressed circulating basal GH levels. What biochemical mechanism drives his rapid linear growth?
opts: Hyperinsulinemia downregulates IGFBP-1 and IGFBP-2, increasing free IGF-1 bioavailability
Adipocytes secrete authentic pituitary growth hormone into the systemic circulation
Elevated leptin binds directly to hepatic somatotroph receptors stimulating gigantism
Aromatization of androgens completely suppresses epiphyseal plate maturation
items.exp: In obesity, increased insulin levels suppress IGFBP-1 and IGFBP-2, increasing free IGF-1 bioavailability and accelerating growth despite low GH. (Book p945)

items.q: Match the physiological regulator to its effect on growth hormone secretion — 1) Hypoglycemia 2) Ghrelin 3) Somatostatin 4) Obesity … A) Stimulates GH release B) Stimulates GH release C) Inhibits GH release D) Inhibits GH release
items.exp: Hypoglycemia, GHRH, and ghrelin stimulate GH; somatostatin, ageing, and obesity inhibit GH secretion. (Book p945)

items.q: What paradoxical hormonal response occurs following TRH administration in patients with acromegaly?
opts: Massive surge of ACTH with acute adrenal crisis
items.exp: In acromegaly, TRH administration produces a paradoxical rise in growth hormone. (Book p945)

items.q: A hypocaloric state or severe malnutrition induces peripheral ___ to growth hormone, resulting in high GH but low IGF-1.
items.exp: Malnutrition and hypocaloric states cause GH resistance with elevated GH and depressed IGF-1. (Book p945)

items.q: Growth hormone exerts its intracellular actions by binding to cell-surface cytokine receptors that signal via:
items.exp: Growth hormone signals through the JAK-STAT cytokine receptor pathway. (Book p945)

items.q: Match the molecule to its circulating half-life — 1) Growth hormone (GH) 2) IGF-1 complexed with IGFBP-3 … A) 5 to 20 minutes B) 12 to 15 hours
items.exp: GH has a short half-life of 5-20 minutes, while IGF-1 bound to IGFBP-3 circulates with a half-life of 12-15 hours. (Book p945)

items.q: Assess regulatory dynamics of growth hormone: I Ghrelin acts as a potent physiological stimulus for GH release. II Ageing is associated with progressive decline and inhibition of GH secretion.
opts: Both I and II are true
Both I and II are false
items.exp: Ghrelin stimulates GH release, while ageing is a recognized inhibitor of GH secretion. (Book p945)
